title: VPC e2e test harness and multiregion egress synthetic probes
author: Anika Shah
content:
Overview

This document describes the VPC end-to-end (E2E) test harness and the synthetic egress probe fleet used to validate multiregion networking, NAT/egress paths, and tenant egress policies for GPU workloads. The harness is intended for CI/CD validation, periodic synthetic audits, and preflight checks prior to capacity migrations or cross-region bursting.

Goals
- Provide automated, repeatable validation of VPC egress correctness across accounts, regions, and peered networks.
- Detect routing regressions, NAT gateway exhaustions, or proxy misconfigurations before they impact serving traffic.
- Offer a terraform-first, reusable test module and CI job templates for teams to include in PR gating.
- Produce actionable telemetry and synthesized findings (pass/fail, latency, failure signature) for SRE and networking teams.

Scope and non-goals
- In scope: NAT/egress connectivity, outbound path correctness (via proxies/egress sidecars), egress bandwidth/throughput sanity, routing failover across regions, and authorization (VPC-level ACLs).
- Out of scope: application layer functional tests, GPU runtime correctness, or per-tenant application logic.

Architecture (text diagram)
- Test controller (GHA/Buildkite) triggers test run -> Terraform test module provisions ephemeral probe runners in target accounts/regions -> Probe runners execute synthetic flows to egress endpoints -> Collector uploads metrics to telemetry (Prometheus remote write / Datadog) -> Alerting/summary posted to Slack and Test Dashboard.

Components
1) Terraform test module (modules/vpc-e2e-probes)
- Produces: ephemeral probe instances (container tasks/ephemeral VMs), IAM roles, ephemeral subnets, and test runner service account.
- Parameters: region, account_id, probe_count, instance_type (t3.micro or f1.small depending on probe load), egress_profile (low/medium/high), attach_metrics_exporter (bool).

2) Probe runner image & harness
- Image contains a small runner (Go binary) that executes a catalog of probes: TCP handshake, TLS negotiation (SNI), HTTP(S) GET/POST, DNS over UDP/TCP, and large UDP datagram tests.
- Runners are rate-limited and emit structured JSON events to stdout and to the collector endpoint.

3) Collector and telemetry
- Collector is an HTTPS endpoint requiring mTLS from runners; it converts events to metrics and traces. Metrics written to Prometheus remote write and Datadog histogram metrics for percentiles.

4) CI integration
- Buildkite and GitHub Actions job templates included in repository for gating changes to networking IaC and runtime.

Test catalog (example table represented in text)
- Probe: http-get 
  - Description: GET to public egress sink (egress-verifier.redwood-infra.net), validates TLS+SNI and public egress path.
  - Thresholds: success >= 99.9% over 1h; p95 latency <= 250ms.
- Probe: nat-exhaustion-check 
  - Description: open 10k ephemeral ports to validation sink and validate connection acceptance rate.
  - Thresholds: connection success >= 98% under small concurrency bursts.
- Probe: proxy-auth 
  - Description: route via egress proxy with mTLS + header auth; validates policy enforcement.
  - Thresholds: 0 auth failures for authorized runners.
- Probe: cross-region-dns 
  - Description: DNS resolution consistency measured across regions.
  - Thresholds: identical A/AAAA responses for configured healthy domains 99.99% of time.

Terraform module usage (example)
- Example invocation snippet (yields ephemeral runners for integration tests):

  module "vpc_e2e_probes" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/infra-test-modules.git//vpc_e2e_probes?ref=v1.2.0"
    region = "us-west-2"
    account_id = "123456789012"
    probe_count = 6
    egress_profile = "low"
    attach_metrics_exporter = true
  }

CI job templates (summary)
1) buildkite/networking-vpc-e2e: runs when network Terraform changes are detected. Steps:
  a) terraform plan (test module only)
  b) terraform apply (ephemeral)
  c) run probes (30m window by default)
  d) collect artifacts and metrics, terraform destroy
  e) post summary to #infra-tests and attach raw events in artifact store.

2) gha/workflows/e2e-egress.yml: short-lived PR gate for small changes (5 probes, 10m runtime).

SLOs and alerting
- Primary SLOs (for synthetic probes):
  - Egress-path availability: 99.95% (24h rolling) measured by http-get and tcp handshake probes.
  - NAT headroom: maintain > 5% ephemeral port headroom for standard NAT pools during peak synthetic runs.
- Alerting rules (examples):
  - SEV2: egress-path availability drops below 99.9% for 15m -> pager to oncall-networking.
  - SEV3: NAT exhaustion anomalies detected (sustained port failure >= 2% for 30m) -> channel #infra-tests and ticket automated.

Data retention and artifacts
- Probe raw events: retained 7 days in object store (s3://redwood-infra-test-artifacts/egress-probes/).
- Summaries & dashboards: 90 days in Datadog/Prometheus-derived dashboards.
- Terraform plan outputs: stored with PR artifacts for 30 days.

Running a manual preflight (runbook)
1) Kick off ephemeral infra via terraform (from laptop or CI):
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-test-modules.git
   - cd infra-test-modules/vpc_e2e_probes && git checkout v1.2.0
   - terraform init && terraform apply -var region=eu-west-1 -var probe_count=8
2) Wait for runners to register (watch logs):
   - buildkite-agent artifact download or curl collector/status endpoint
3) Start a focused test run: POST /api/v1/tests/run with body {"suite":"preflight","duration_minutes":20} (example client included in repo).
4) Collect results: curl https://collector.redwood-infra.net/api/v1/results?run_id=...
5) On success: terraform destroy -auto-approve. On failure: archive artifacts and open ticket with artifacts link.

CI cost controls and safety knobs
- Default probe_count per region = 4, max 20 (module enforces max via variable validation).
- Circuit breaker: if any account's egress error rate > 10% in the last 5m for two consecutive windows, the controller will stop new runs for that account and notify.

Security considerations
- Runners use ephemeral service accounts with least-privilege IAM policies; no secrets are stored on instances.
- Collector requires mTLS and only accepts connections from the runner subnet CIDR ranges in the ephemeral stack.
- All test artifacts are scanned for PII before being exposed externally.

Telemetry & dashboards (owners)
- Dashboard: Infra / VPC E2E Probes (owner: networking-team). Panels:
  - Egress success rate (p99/p95/p50) by region/account.
  - Average egress latency by probe type.
  - NAT port headroom and exhaustion events.
  - Recent failure signatures with top 10 stack traces.

Ownership and run cadence
- Owner: networking-team (primary), eng-sre (secondary), infra-ci (support).
- Scheduled synthetic runs: every 30 minutes for critical regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1), every 2 hours for secondary regions.
- On-call rotation to triage synthetic SEV2 alerts: networking oncall.

Rollout and migration instructions (for migrating VPCs or changing NAT topology)
1) Add vpc_e2e_probes module to migration plan PR and run with probe_count=6 for target and control regions.
2) Run smoke tests (5 minutes) and verify critical probes pass before cutover.
3) If failures observed, rollback network changes. Capture artifacts and notify networking oncall.

Common failure modes and remediation (troubleshooting)
- Failure: TLS handshake errors from multiple runners in single AZ.
  - Likely: egress proxy cert rotation or outdated trust bundle.
  - Remediation: check proxy certs, refresh trust store, rerun probes.
- Failure: DNS discrepancy across regions.
  - Likely: Resolver configuration or Route53 failover misconfig.
  - Remediation: compare resolvers, run dig from runners, check Route53 health checks.
- Failure: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion.
  - Likely: underprovisioned NAT gateway or shared NAT for too many tenants.
  - Remediation: small-scale increase in NAT pool or enable shared egress ENI autoscaling.

Onboarding checklist for teams
- Add module invocation to your migration branch and set attach_metrics_exporter = true.
- Add a CI job using the provided Buildkite/GHA templates.
- Confirm runner IAM role and VPC peer permissions with networking-team.
- Run the harness in a non-production account and inspect dashboards before running in production.

Appendix: CLI snippets and commands
- Kick off a quick adhoc run (example):
  export RUNNER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/redwood-inference/probe-runner:v1.2.0
  buildkite-agent pipeline upload .buildkite/pipelines/vpc-e2e.yml

- Inspect logs from a runner instance (example):
  aws ssm start-session --target i-0123456789abcdef0 --document-name AWS-StartInteractiveCommand --parameters 'command=["sudo journalctl -u probe-runner -f"]'

Notes
- The module is versioned and pinned; changes to the probe runner must include a schema migration note.
- When adding new probes, include simulated failure modes and remediation guidance in the probe's test definition.
